title: Paffett wins at home from pole at Brands Hatch
dek: Gary Paffett won the third DTM round from pole for HWA Mercedes, 5.065 seconds ahead of Bruno Spengler's BMW, with Mike Rockenfeller's Audi making it a podium for all three makes.

chapters.title: A British round with the title race already shuffled
text: The third of the ten races in the 2012 DTM season was staged at Brands Hatch on Sunday 20 May, after two opening rounds in Germany at the Hockenheimring and the Lausitzring. In the first year of the BMW M3 DTM's return, the order had already been shaken up twice. Gary Paffett opened the year with a win for HWA Mercedes from sixth on the grid, while Bruno Spengler, who had retired after three laps at Hockenheim, took the Lausitzring victory from pole with Paffett 1.019 seconds behind in second.

That left Paffett arriving in Britain as the points leader on 43, with fellow Mercedes driver Jamie Green on 30 and Mattias Ekström and Spengler level on 25. For Paffett it was a home race, and Andy Priaulx was another British driver in BMW's line-up. BMW Motorsport Director Jens Marquardt would say after the race that the three manufacturers were on a par and that the pack had been reshuffled at every circuit so far, which made the weekends close to impossible to predict.

The grid was a full 22 cars, eight Audis, eight Mercedes and six BMWs, and Brands Hatch was the first of the season's rounds to be held outside Germany. Audi had yet to win in 2012, with both opening rounds going to other makes, and Brands Hatch was a short 1.929-kilometre track where the three makes would again be measured against each other.

chapters.title: Paffett takes a home pole, Mercedes lock out the front row
text: Paffett took pole position on Saturday with a lap of 41.266, 0.144 seconds quicker than his HWA team-mate Christian Vietoris on 41.410, which gave Mercedes the whole front row. Spengler made the four-car final session and was third on 41.462, just 0.052 seconds behind Vietoris, with Mike Rockenfeller's Phoenix Audi fourth on 41.484, a mere 0.022 seconds behind the BMW. All three makes were therefore represented in the first two rows.

Martin Tomczyk was fifth in the RMG BMW, Filipe Albuquerque sixth in a Rosberg Audi and Adrien Tambay seventh in the Abt Audi, ahead of Ekström in eighth. Augusto Farfus was ninth for BMW and Green tenth, the last of the six drivers who went out before the final shoot-out.

Behind them Edoardo Mortara was 11th, Miguel Molina 12th, Joey Hand 13th and Priaulx 14th, with Timo Scheider only 15th. Dirk Werner, Schnitzer's second driver, was 19th, David Coulthard 20th and Susie Wolff 21st, while Rahel Frey was 22nd on 41.956. The field was packed tightly, with less than nine tenths of a second covering the best times of all 22 cars.

chapters.title: Spengler gets up to second, Tomczyk fights back
text: Paffett led away from pole, but the front row did not stay intact. Vietoris lost places on the opening lap from the outside of the front row, and Spengler, with a very good start from third on the grid, went straight into second place in the BMW. From there he stayed close to the leader through the first stint, with Paffett slowly building a margin.

Tomczyk had a poorer start and dropped two places, but he recovered quickly, passing Tambay's Abt Audi within a lap or two and then working his way past Ekström. Contact early on broke the front of Priaulx's RBM BMW; the damage and an unscheduled tyre stop left him unable to continue, and he was out after 12 laps, the first car out of the race.

chapters.title: Two stops, traffic and an engine problem
text: The leaders made two stops each, and the stops decided several places. Spengler called his second stop particularly good, and a quicker pit stop than Paffett's helped him close the gap between them in the second half of the race. Tomczyk said his own stops were not quite perfect but still gained a place through strategy.

Farfus had a frustrating afternoon. He made both of his stops ahead of the others, but came out in traffic each time and then spent a long stretch stuck behind Tambay's Audi, which his team felt it was clearly quicker than. Scheider, who had started 15th, pulled out after 55 laps with an engine problem.

chapters.title: Paffett wins by 5.065 seconds as Spengler holds off Rockenfeller
text: Paffett completed the 97 laps in 1:10:01.585 and crossed the line 5.065 seconds clear of Spengler. The BMW's front splitter had been damaged on the kerb at the first corner, which cost it downforce, particularly in right-hand corners, and Spengler could not keep pushing in the closing laps. Rockenfeller closed on him lap after lap but finished only 0.514 seconds behind in third, with Tomczyk a further 0.418 seconds back in fourth. Tomczyk, who also set the fastest lap, a 42.138 on lap 57, took his best result of the year.

Ekström was fifth, 22.416 seconds behind the winner, ahead of Vietoris, who recovered from his poor start to take sixth. Molina climbed from 12th on the grid to seventh, Green was eighth and Mortara and Albuquerque finished ninth and tenth. Farfus took 11th place, one place ahead of Tambay. Hand was 13th and Robert Wickens 14th, the last cars on the lead lap, while Coulthard, Werner, Roberto Merhi, Frey and Ralf Schumacher followed a lap down. Wolff was classified 20th, 16 laps behind, and Scheider and Priaulx were the only retirements.

chapters.title: Paffett stretches the lead to 25 points
text: Paffett called it a perfect race that the team had controlled from start to finish. The win, his second of the season, took him to 68 points and put him 25 clear of Spengler, who moved up to second on 43. Ekström was third on 35, Green fourth on 34 and Rockenfeller fifth on 25. For Spengler it was a second podium in as many races, and he said that Paffett had been very quick in the first stint but that he had managed to stay on his tail, even if the broken splitter made the finish tense.

BMW left Britain content. Marquardt praised the second and fourth places as fantastic results and said the drivers had found their feet very quickly. Team principal Charly Lamm said Spengler had been lacking downforce towards the end, and Tomczyk looked ahead with confidence even though he felt the result could have been better. RBM had a worse day: Priaulx was forced out early and Farfus finished 11th after being slowed by traffic, with team principal Bart Mampaey saying the team had learned a lot in its first year.

Audi saw the weekend as encouraging. Wolfgang Ullrich said five cars in the top ten were a strong overall team result which showed that Audi was on the right track, and he looked ahead to the next races with confidence. Rockenfeller was more cautious, saying that Brands Hatch was not the same as Hockenheim or the Lausitzring and that he would only know that Audi had taken a step forward if he finished third at the Red Bull Ring too. Hans-Jürgen Abt, whose Ekström was more than 20 seconds behind the winner, said it was not a successful weekend from the Abt Sportsline point of view and that victory was the aim.

The next round was the Red Bull Ring at Spielberg on Sunday 3 June, two weeks later. Marquardt said that BMW barely had time to catch its breath and hoped to be as quick in Austria as it had been in Britain, while Rockenfeller was already looking to the Austrian round as the real test of the work Audi had done since the start of the season.

facts.v: Paffett's Mercedes won by 5.065 seconds from Spengler's BMW, with Rockenfeller's Audi 0.514 seconds further back in third.
